logo_override.validation_detail: webfetch of the asset URL returned 'Image fetched successfully' (HTTP 200 + image content type, not HTML). WP REST media record id=2661 (slug ai-logo-horizontal_colour, title 'AI LOGO HORIZONTAL_COLOUR') confirms mime_type=image/jpeg and media_details 2560x334 for the -scaled file. Rendered output shows the full Alberta Innovates horizontal primary wordmark: navy 'ALBERTA INNOVATES' lettering plus the three-strand triangular ribbon mark in green/cyan/navy on an opaque white field. Colour and mark geometry match the live inline header SVG on the site (fills #003a70 wordmark, #00b189 green, #00abd9 cyan), confirming it is the same brand asset rather than a different body's logo. Because it is a JPEG it cannot be white-on-transparent, and the rendered pixels confirm dark/coloured artwork.

notes: Site is WordPress (Yoast SEO, theme 'abinnovates') and webfetch was not blocked, so no Playwright fallback was needed. Both https://albertainnovates.ca/ and the shard page https://albertainnovates.ca/programs/graduate-student-scholarships (canonical: https://albertainnovates.ca/funding/graduate-student-scholarships/) were fetched and scanned. Neither page exposes a logo via og:image or a schema.org 'logo' property - the Yoast ld+json graph contains only WebPage/BreadcrumbList/WebSite nodes - and no with 'logo' in its src exists anywhere in either document. All /icon references in are the same-origin WordPress favicon crops (https://albertainnovates.ca/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/cropped-favicon-{32x32,192x192,180x180,270x270}.png, also the msapplication-TileImage), which are the small icon mark only, not the wordmark, so they were not used. The live header and footer logos are BOTH inline
